Compare model structures

Source: R/compare_structures.R
compare_structures.Rd

Calibrates several model structures in exactly the same way and ranks them by their headline score on the validation window, which no calibration saw. Each structure is logged as an ordinary structure_selected entry and an auto_calibration entry, linked by a shared comparison id, so the comparison is part of the audit trail and structure_comparison() can rebuild the ranking from the log at any time.

Usage

compare_structures(
  project,
  structures = NULL,
  overrides = NULL,
  exclude = NULL,
  objective = c("nse", "rmse", "log_rmse"),
  starts = 3L,
  seed = 1,
  control = list(maxit = 200),
  method = c("lbfgsb", "nelder_mead"),
  cores = 1L,
  cross_validate = FALSE,
  reasoning
)

structure_comparison(project, comparison = NULL)

Arguments

project

Path of a calibration project with registered data and a validation window.

structures

Named list of configurations; by default structure_set(), built on the project's latest structure if there is one. Each is given the project's area.

overrides, exclude

Passed to calibration_bounds() for every structure.

objective, starts, seed, control, method

Passed to calibrate_pdm().

cores

Number of parallel worker processes; 1 runs in this session.

cross_validate

If TRUE, also calibrate on the validation window and score on the calibration window.

reasoning

Why the comparison is being run.

comparison

A comparison id; by default the latest comparison in the project.

Value

compare_structures() and structure_comparison(): a data.table ranked best first, with rank, structure, parameters, calibration and validation (headline scores), change (validation minus calibration), cross_validated when requested, evaluations, starts_agree, and the two entry ids.

Details

Every structure gets the bounds from calibration_bounds() for its components, with log-scale search where the table says so, and the same objective, starts, seed and iteration limit. A structure with more parameters nearly always fits the calibration window better; the ranking uses the validation window instead, and the table shows how much each structure's score changes between the two. A large drop is the mark of a structure buying its fit with parameters.

With cross_validate = TRUE, each structure is also calibrated on the validation window and scored on the calibration window, and ranked on the mean of the two held-out scores. This is more robust for short records, and doubles the cost.

Choosing a structure on the validation window uses that window; the optional test window of register_data(), scored once by test_candidate(), then gives an untouched final check.

See also

structure_set(), calibration_bounds(), calibration_log
